title: One of the creatures for my game — made with Codex + Blender + Godot
author: SalivaSpittingWorm
selftext:
I’m working on my own game, though it’s still early days. I’ll share more about it once I have a proper gameplay demo to show.

For now, here’s one of the creatures that will inhabit the world. I’ve been working on its animations, trying to give this little guy some weight and personality.

What do you think? Any movements that look off to you?

comments.author: yaxir
comments.body:
Fantastic. Thank you for sharing this. Would you happen to know of any more solid stuff like this but for, let's say, fine pixel art or dense arcade graphics?

I'm having trouble having proper animations and movement for pixel art, not the rough crude pixel art but beautiful very fine finally drawn pixel art being animated. I don't know how to animate them properly. I'm trying with Ludo and I'm struggling.

Would you prefer or recommend something like Meshy or Tripo that can then be rendered onto the 2D pixel dimensions or something like that? Any advice is appreciated

replies.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
replies.body: Not sure how much I can help with this one, I had to ask Codex My only idea was pretty much what you suggested — make a 3D model, animate it, then render it with a pixel art look into a sprite sheet. Codex also suggested [PixelLab](https://www.pixellab.ai/), where you upload your sprite and tell it what movement you want, and [Scenario’s Pixel Lock](https://www.scenario.com/apps/pixel-lock-character-to-sprite-sheet), which makes more detailed pixel art idle animations. I haven’t tried either myself, but maybe one of those could help :)

comments.author: JaironKalach
comments.body: So adorable. What was your workflow for the animations?

replies.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
replies.body: First, based on my rough sketch, I had GPTchat turn it into a proper image. Then we made images from all angles. Next, I sent it to Meshy so he could create a 3D model and a skeleton for me. Then I sent it to Codex and came up with movement ideas, inspired by animal movements. A dwarf pony and an elephant turtle. I gave those as reference models to Codex, and he animated them in Blender. Some of the movements weren’t very good, so it took a few revisions, but I’m pretty happy with the final result. :)

replies.author: JaironKalach
replies.body: I thanks for the response. I think you should be happy. Did you give actual reference videos to codex or just descriptions of the movement? What model did you use? I ask, because my one attempt at animation left my character just moving very awkwardly, so I know I’m not giving the right reference material.

replies.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
replies.body: I had an animation sheet created to show exactly how and what should move as the character moves. I provided a written description and also sent Codex to watch a video showing the movements of the specific animals I had in mind. It actually worked pretty well. :)

replies.author: JaironKalach
replies.body: So you (and codex) did a set of key frame images as well as videos of your references and your textual description? That makes sense.

replies.author: SalivaSpittingWorm
replies.body: Exactly. And it still needed a few fixes after that, but not many. :)
